MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #19
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What number is the Roman numeral VIII? (1 mark)
   A. 8
   B. 1
   C. 2
   D. 3

2. Which of these is a multiple of 8? (1 mark)
   A. 71
   B. 74
   C. 72
   D. 73

3. Which Roman numeral stands for 6? (1 mark)
   A. VIIII
   B. VI
   C. VX
   D. IIII

4. Which Roman numeral stands for 8? (1 mark)
   A. VX
   B. VIIII
   C. IIII
   D. VIII

5. Which of these shows 583 in words? (1 mark)
   A. five hundred and ninety-three
   B. five hundred and eighty-three
   C. six hundred and eighty-three
   D. five hundred and thirty-eight

6. A school has 1,845 pupils in the lower classes and 2,367 pupils in the upper classes. How many pupils are in the school? (1 mark)
   A. 4,212 pupils
   B. 3,102 pupils
   C. 4,312 pupils
   D. 4,202 pupils

7. Estimate 2,694 + 3,158 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 5,952
   B. 5,860
   C. 5,850
   D. 5,840

8. How many times do you need to regroup when you add 2,999 + 3,001? (1 mark)
   A. 1
   B. 2
   C. 3
   D. 0

9. A farmer picked 1,275 mangoes on Monday and 3,548 mangoes on Tuesday. How many mangoes did he pick? (1 mark)
   A. 4,713 mangoes
   B. 4,823 mangoes
   C. 4,813 mangoes
   D. 4,923 mangoes

10. Work out 1,204 + 1,315. (1 mark)
   A. 2,519
   B. 2,529
   C. 2,419
   D. 3,519

11. Work out 7,300 − 4,562. (1 mark)
   A. 2,638
   B. 2,738
   C. 3,262
   D. 2,748

12. Work out 7,000 − 3,456. (1 mark)
   A. 3,444
   B. 3,544
   C. 3,554
   D. 4,456

13. What is 18 × 50? (1 mark)
   A. 68
   B. 9,000
   C. 900
   D. 90

14. Which division fact belongs to the same family as 9 × 5 = 45? (1 mark)
   A. 45 ÷ 9 = 9
   B. 45 ÷ 45 = 9
   C. 45 ÷ 9 = 5
   D. 5 ÷ 9 = 45

15. What is 91 ÷ 7? (1 mark)
   A. 14
   B. 12
   C. 13
   D. 23

16. What is 56 ÷ 8? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 8
   C. 6
   D. 17

17. What is 700 ÷ 100? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 700
   C. 70
   D. 8

18. Dan writes another set of fractions. Which of these is a mixed fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 4 2/3
   B. 8/3
   C. 1/2
   D. 11/5

19. What is 1/4 of 36? (1 mark)
   A. 9
   B. 27
   C. 18
   D. 5

20. Change 22/7 to a mixed fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 3 2/7
   B. 4 1/7
   C. 1 3/7
   D. 3 1/7

21. In the fraction 2/9, which number is the denominator? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 2
   C. 9
   D. 11

22. A circle is cut into 12 equal parts and 5 parts are shaded. What fraction is not shaded? (1 mark)
   A. 7/12
   B. 12/7
   C. 7/5
   D. 5/12

23. Write 45/100 as a decimal. (1 mark)
   A. 4.5
   B. 0.045
   C. 0.45
   D. 0.54

24. Which expression shows "the sum of a and 9"? (1 mark)
   A. a + 9
   B. a ÷ 9
   C. a − 9
   D. 9a

25. Which expression shows "twice a number p"? (1 mark)
   A. 2p
   B. p − 2
   C. p + 2
   D. p ÷ 2

26. A matatu carries m passengers. Eight get in and three get out. Which expression shows the number of passengers now? (1 mark)
   A. m − 5
   B. m + 5
   C. m + 11
   D. 8m − 3

27. A rope 7 m 20 cm long is cut into 6 equal pieces. How long is each piece? (1 mark)
   A. 2 m 40 cm
   B. 7 m 14 cm
   C. 1 m 20 cm
   D. 1 m 30 cm

28. What is 3 m 45 cm + 2 m 80 cm? (1 mark)
   A. 7 m 25 cm
   B. 5 m 25 cm
   C. 6 m 25 cm
   D. 6 m 15 cm

29. A rope 5 m 25 cm long is cut into 3 equal pieces. How long is each piece? (1 mark)
   A. 1 m 75 cm
   B. 5 m 22 cm
   C. 3 m 50 cm
   D. 1 m 85 cm

30. A rectangle is made of 10 rows with 10 unit squares in each row. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 20 square units
   B. 110 square units
   C. 100 square units
   D. 40 square units

31. A cuboid is 5 blocks long, 4 blocks wide and 4 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 20 blocks
   B. 80 blocks
   C. 13 blocks
   D. 85 blocks

32. A shop sells 3 packets of milk of 1/2 L each. What is the total amount of milk? (1 mark)
   A. 2 L
   B. 1 1/2 L
   C. 3 L
   D. 1 L

33. A basket of mangoes has a mass of 8 kg. The empty basket has a mass of 1 1/2 kg. What is the mass of the mangoes? (1 mark)
   A. 6 kg
   B. 6 1/2 kg
   C. 9 1/2 kg
   D. 7 kg

34. Change 48 hours to days. (1 mark)
   A. 0.8 days
   B. 2 days
   C. 3 days
   D. 4 days

35. Change 270 minutes to hours and minutes. (1 mark)
   A. 5 h 30 min
   B. 4 h 30 min
   C. 4 h
   D. 5 h

36. Change 90 minutes to hours and minutes. (1 mark)
   A. 1 h
   B. 1 h 30 min
   C. 2 h 30 min
   D. 2 h

37. One unit costs Ksh 250. What is the cost of 4 bottles of cooking oil? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 1,000
   B. Ksh 1,010
   C. Ksh 254
   D. Ksh 750

38. What does the size of an angle depend on? (1 mark)
   A. How far apart the arms are
   B. How long the arms are
   C. The colour of the arms
   D. The number of arms

39. A quarter turn makes (1 mark)
   A. no angle
   B. a straight line
   C. a right angle
   D. a full turn

40. The table shows the type of transport 10 pupils use to come to school: walking 6, bicycle 2, bus 1, car 1. What is the total of all the numbers? (1 mark)
   A. 12
   B. 9
   C. 10
   D. 11

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. A stack of soda crates has 5 crates along the wall, 4 crates deep and 4 layers high. How many crates are in the stack? (3 marks)

42. Name three objects in your classroom that have right angles. (3 marks)

43. Explain why 2a + 3b cannot be written as 5ab. (2 marks)

44. Two runners finish a race in 12.4 seconds and 12.35 seconds. Who is faster? Explain. (3 marks)

45. Work out 36 × 24 by first multiplying by the ones and then by the tens. (3 marks)

46. Round 47, 342 and 995 to the nearest ten. (3 marks)

47. In the number 27,150, give the place value and the total value of the digit 7. (4 marks)

48. Work out 4,000 − 1,236. Show how you regroup. (3 marks)

49. Write instructions for a person to walk from the classroom door to the school gate using at least two turns. Use words such as forward, quarter turn, clockwise and anticlockwise. (4 marks)

50. Name the plane figure of each object: a plate, a floor tile, a door. (3 marks)

51. A learner says the volume of a cuboid 4 blocks long, 3 wide and 2 high is 9 blocks because 4 + 3 + 2 = 9. What mistake did the learner make and what is the correct volume? (3 marks)

52. A farmer has 95 eggs to pack into trays that each hold 6 eggs. (a) How many full trays are there and how many eggs are left over? (b) How many trays are needed to pack all the eggs? (5 marks)

53. Describe how the length of a shadow changes from morning to afternoon and explain how this can help us to estimate the time of day. (4 marks)

54. Explain how you can compare the areas of two sheets of paper without using a ruler. (2 marks)

55. Amina says the area of a rectangle with 4 rows and 6 columns is 10 because 4 + 6 = 10. Explain her mistake and give the correct area. (3 marks)

56. Write the steps for collecting and recording data about the favourite colours of 10 friends. (4 marks)

57. A stadium seats 9,000 people. During a match 6,450 seats are taken. How many seats are empty? (3 marks)

58. A group of five tallies and 3 more tally marks show which number? Explain how you count. (2 marks)

59. Complete the pattern 3, 6, 12, 24, ... with the next two numbers and state the rule. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #19 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — 8
   VIII stands for 8.

2. C — 72
   72 = 8 × 9, so 72 is a multiple of 8.

3. B — VI
   6 is written VI. Letters after a bigger letter are added.

4. D — VIII
   8 is written VIII. Letters after a bigger letter are added.

5. B — five hundred and eighty-three
   583 = five hundred and eighty-three. Say the hundreds, then "and", then the tens and ones.

6. A — 4,212 pupils
   Add 1,845 + 2,367 = 4,212 pupils.

7. C — 5,850
   2,694 rounds to 2,690 and 3,158 rounds to 3,160. 2,690 + 3,160 = 5,850.

8. C — 3
   Check each column from the right for a total of 10 or more, remembering the carried digit. 2,999 + 3,001 needs 3 regroupings.

9. B — 4,823 mangoes
   Add 1,275 + 3,548 = 4,823 mangoes.

10. A — 2,519
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 1,204 + 1,315 = 2,519.

11. B — 2,738
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 7,300 − 4,562 = 2,738. Check: 2,738 + 4,562 = 7,300.

12. B — 3,544
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 7,000 − 3,456 = 3,544. Check: 3,544 + 3,456 = 7,000.

13. C — 900
   18 × 5 = 90, then × 10 gives 900.

14. C — 45 ÷ 9 = 5
   Division undoes multiplication. Since 9 × 5 = 45, we know 45 ÷ 9 = 5 and 45 ÷ 5 = 9.

15. C — 13
   7 × 13 = 91, so 91 ÷ 7 = 13.

16. A — 7
   8 × 7 = 56, so 56 ÷ 8 = 7.

17. A — 7
   Dividing by 100 removes two zeros. 700 ÷ 100 = 7.

18. A — 4 2/3
   A mixed fraction has a whole number and a proper fraction, like 4 2/3.

19. A — 9
   36 ÷ 4 = 9 and 9 × 1 = 9. So 1/4 of 36 is 9.

20. D — 3 1/7
   22 ÷ 7 = 3 remainder 1. The whole number is 3 and the fraction is 1/7, so 22/7 = 3 1/7.

21. C — 9
   The denominator is the bottom number. It shows how many equal parts the whole is cut into.

22. A — 7/12
   Not shaded: 12 − 5 = 7 parts, so 7/12.

23. C — 0.45
   Tenths need one digit after the decimal point and hundredths need two digits. 45/100 = 0.45.

24. A — a + 9
   The key words tell us the operation. "the sum of a and 9" is written a + 9.

25. A — 2p
   The key words tell us the operation. "twice a number p" is written 2p.

26. B — m + 5
   m + 8 − 3 = m + 5.

27. C — 1 m 20 cm
   720 ÷ 6 = 120 cm = 1 m 20 cm.

28. C — 6 m 25 cm
   Change to centimetres: 345 + 280 = 625 cm = 6 m 25 cm.

29. A — 1 m 75 cm
   525 ÷ 3 = 175 cm = 1 m 75 cm.

30. C — 100 square units
   Area = rows × columns = 10 × 10 = 100 square units.

31. B — 80 blocks
   One layer has 5 × 4 = 20 blocks. There are 4 layers, so the volume is 20 × 4 = 80 blocks.

32. B — 1 1/2 L
   3 × 1/2 = 3/2 = 1 1/2 L.

33. B — 6 1/2 kg
   8 − 1 1/2 = 6 1/2 kg.

34. B — 2 days
   48 ÷ 24 = 2 days.

35. B — 4 h 30 min
   270 ÷ 60 = 4 remainder 30, so 270 minutes = 4 h 30 min.

36. B — 1 h 30 min
   90 ÷ 60 = 1 remainder 30, so 90 minutes = 1 h 30 min.

37. A — Ksh 1,000
   Cost = number × price = 4 × 250 = Ksh 1,000.

38. A — How far apart the arms are
   The size depends on the opening between the arms, not on their length.

39. C — a right angle
   A quarter turn sweeps out a right angle.

40. C — 10
   Add all the numbers: 6 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 10.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: 80 crates
   Working / marking points: 5 × 4 = 20 per layer (1 mark); 20 × 4 (1 mark); 80 crates (1 mark).

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Any three correct, for example a window, a door and a book.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct object.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: a and b are different, so 2a and 3b are not like terms and cannot be joined.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for unlike terms and 1 mark for the reason.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: The runner with 12.35 seconds is faster. 12.4 = 12.40, and 12.35 is less than 12.40, so it took less time.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for writing 12.4 as 12.40, 1 mark for comparing, 1 mark for the correct runner.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: 864
   Working / marking points: 36 × 4 = 144 (1 mark); 36 × 20 = 720 (1 mark); 144 + 720 = 864 (1 mark).

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: 50, 340 and 1,000
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct rounding. 995 goes up to 1,000 because the ones digit is 5.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: Place value: thousands. Total value: 7 × 1,000 = 7,000.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for thousands; 1 mark for 7 × 1,000; 1 mark for the answer 7,000; 1 mark for clear working.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2,764
   Working / marking points: Borrow from the thousands so the number is 3 thousands 9 hundreds 9 tens 10 ones (1 mark). 10 − 6 = 4, 9 − 3 = 6, 9 − 2 = 7, 3 − 1 = 2 (1 mark). Answer 2,764 (1 mark).

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: Walk forward 10 steps. Make a quarter turn clockwise. Walk forward 5 steps. Make a quarter turn anticlockwise. Walk to the gate.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the first move with steps, 1 mark for a turn with its size, 1 mark for the turn direction, 1 mark for clear order.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Plate: circle. Floor tile: square. Door: rectangle.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct shape.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: The learner added. She should multiply: one layer has 4 × 3 = 12 blocks and 2 layers make 24 blocks.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the mistake, 1 mark for the method, 1 mark for 24 blocks.

52. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 15 full trays and 5 eggs left over (b) 16 trays
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for 95 ÷ 6 = 15 remainder 5, 1 mark for stating both, 1 mark for the leftover eggs needing another tray, 1 mark for 16.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: In the morning shadows are long, they get shorter towards midday when they are very short, and then get longer again in the afternoon. A very short shadow means it is about midday.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for long in the morning, 1 mark for short at midday, 1 mark for long again in the afternoon, 1 mark for estimating time.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: Put one sheet on top of the other with their corners lined up. The sheet that sticks out has the bigger area.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for placing one on the other and 1 mark for saying the one that sticks out is bigger.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: She added the rows and columns. Area is rows × columns = 4 × 6 = 24 square units.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying she added, 1 mark for saying multiply, 1 mark for 24.

56. (4 marks)
   Answer: Decide the question; ask each friend and make a tally mark; draw a table with a title and headings; write the totals and check they add up to 10.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2,550 seats
   Working / marking points: 9,000 − 6,450 with regrouping across zeros. 1 mark for the setup, 1 mark for regrouping, 1 mark for the answer with units.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: 8. Count the group of five as 5, then add 3 more: 5 + 3 = 8.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 8 and 1 mark for the explanation.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: Rule: multiply by 2. Next numbers: 48 and 96.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the rule, 1 mark for each correct number.
